paper text.text:
Suppose next that $B$ is planar, and write $x,y,t$ for its
attachments. First suppose its three single-edge completions are
planar. Its triangle completion contains the nonplanar two-edge
completions, so it is nonplanar. It is not $V_8$, as it contains a triangle. Halin's theorem and
Lemma~\ref{core:three-root-setup} give a three-cut $X$ of the
triangle completion and two vertices of $\operatorname{Int}(B)$
with neighborhood $X$.
By observation (a) in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{r2:three-mark-entrance}, adding an edge between
attachments in $X$ does not change planarity, so two attachments
in $X$ would give a planar two-edge completion.
If $X$ contains exactly one attachment, say $x$, and $y,t$ lie in
one component of $B-X$, that component is already adjacent in $B$
to both vertices of $X-\{x\}$: its neighborhood in the triangle
completion is $X$, and the added triangle edges leaving it
can only end at $x$. Adding $xy$ therefore makes it adjacent
to all of $X$, contradicting planarity. If they lie separately, $xy,xt$
affect different bridges, so their separate planarity makes
$B+xy+xt$ planar. Thus $X\subseteq\operatorname{Int}(B)$, and
$X$ is a twin triple disjoint from $\{a,b,c\}$, contrary to the
assumption of this section.

So some single-edge completion, say $B+xy$, is nonplanar.
Lemma~\ref{r2:three-mark-entrance} gives a
$K_{3,3}$ subdivision $H\subseteq B+xy$ with $H-xy+xt+yt$
nonplanar. Apply Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with
$E=\{xy\}$. It gives a shortened subdivision $H'$ with the same
attachment positions, so $H'-xy+xt+yt$ remains nonplanar by
Lemma~\ref{r2:position-of-third}. The other two completions
contain $H'$. Thus $B$ equals this allowed minor.

Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists the nonplanar
forms by placing the three attachments on or outside the
subdivision, shortening its paths, and adding the edges required
to connect its interior and give every attachment an interior
neighbor. It lists the planar forms in the same way with the
added edge $xy$, taking each pair of attachments as $x,y$, and we
keep those whose three two-edge completions are nonplanar. Combine each form with
$\Psi_2$ and a vertex $v$, taking each of the three other triples
as $N(v)$ in turn. These six choices give $5{,}934$ graphs,
recorded in~\supp{E19}.
For each graph the record gives a cut of at most two vertices,
five branch sets giving a $K_5$ minor, or an edge deletion or
contraction giving a nontoroidal proper minor.
Each outcome contradicts a defining property of $G$.
\end{proof}

vertex names: Psi_2: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with {a,b,d}; v is the contracted other component. Interior vertices of U are u0, u1, ....
cases: U on T = {a,c,d} or {b,c,d}, and N(v) each of the three other triples: six cases.

nonplanar U.construction: Construction 3.16 with attachments T and no added edges

planar U.construction: Construction 3.16 with attachments T and one added edge xy, required, for each pair xy of T; kept when planar with all three two-edge completions nonplanar; merged over the three pairs up to isomorphism fixing T
